title: The Decameron
author: Giovanni Boccaccio
current_text: The Decameron was placed on the Index of 1559 under the instructions of Paul IV, and its prohibition was confirmed in the Index of 1564.

sources.quote: An instance of a book the censorship of which caused no little difficulty to the authorities of the Index is afforded by the _Decameron_ of Boccaccio. The book had, under the instructions of Paul IV, been placed upon the Index of 1559, and the prohibition was confirmed in that of 1564.
sources.title: CHAPTER IX | The censorship of the Church of Rome and its influence upon the production and distribution of literature, volume 2 (of 2)

ban_rows.note: Listed on the Index Librorum Prohibitorum from its first edition in 1559. The Church objected to explicit sexual content and to Boccaccio's satirical portrayals of lecherous clergy. A bowdlerised edition approved for Catholic readers replaced monks with "hermits" and abbesses with "noblewomen." The unexpurgated text remained banned until 1966.
In 1939 a NZ magistrate found the Decameron indecent in a prosecution of a lending-library owner; the finding was overturned on appeal later that year.

Boccaccio's medieval novella collection was named in independent reporting on a list of roughly 252 titles pulled from major Russian online retailers in late 2024 under Russia's expanded "LGBT propaganda" law.
